2.4.1.4-r1.burton_quote: If it be either carried about, or taken in a potion, it will increase wisdom, saith Cardan, expel fear; he brags that he hath cured many madmen with it, which when they laid by the stone, were as mad again as ever they were at first

2.4.1.4-r2.burton_quote: avails much against fantastic illusions which proceed from melancholy

2.4.1.4-r3.burton_quote: which drive away childish fears, Devils, overcome sorrow, and hung about the neck repress troublesome dreams

2.4.1.4-r4.burton_quote: fairest of all precious stones, of sky colour, and a great enemy to black choler, frees the mind, mends manners

2.4.1.4-r5.burton_quote: That almost all Jewels and precious stones, have excellent virtues to pacify the affections of the mind, for which cause rich men so much covet to have them

2.4.1.4-r6.burton_quote: and those smaller Unions which are found in shells amongst the Persians and Indians, by the consent of all writers, are very cordial

2.4.1.4-r8.burton_quote: a drop of his preparations should go farther than a dram, or ounce of theirs

2.4.1.4-r9.burton_quote: no man can be an excellent Physician that hath not some skill in Chemistical distillations, and that Chronic diseases can hardly be cured without mineral medicines
2.4.1.4-r9.translation: or where the blood is corrupted.
